evidence.claim: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional text; directly states presidential powers and military command relation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro held this office throughout 2022; the source is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Legal authority does not show how Bolsonaro used it in nuclear or existential-risk matters.

evidence.claim: Brazil voted for the Security Council draft condemning the Russian invasion, but Bolsonaro had recently met Putin, said he was in solidarity with Russia, and later said Putin had peaceful intentions.
evidence.title: Despite Bolsonaro reluctance, Brazil votes against Russia on U.N. resolution
evidence.excerpt: Brazil voted for the Security Council draft condemning the Russian invasion, but Bolsonaro had recently met Putin, said he was in solidarity with Russia, and later said Putin had peaceful intentions.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and lines 666-677 in the article view
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting carried by Euronews; strong independent journalism, but still secondary.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the opening week of the invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro conduct on the Putin trip; the vote itself was a government action under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: Brazil still voted against Russia at the UN despite Bolsonaro's remarks, so the article shows mixed rather than one-directional conduct.

evidence.claim: Brazil sent a FAB KC-390 to evacuate about 70 people from the Ukraine crisis and also sent 11.6 tons of humanitarian donations for the Ukrainian population.
evidence.title: Governo Federal vai resgatar cerca de 70 pessoas que deixaram a Ucrânia
evidence.excerpt: Brazil sent a FAB KC-390 to evacuate about 70 people from the Ukraine crisis and also sent 11.6 tons of humanitarian donations for the Ukrainian population.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government operational report on a contemporaneous repatriation and aid mission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under Bolsonaro's presidency; not personal command evidence.
contrary_evidence: This is humanitarian support, not an independent measure of strategic peace leadership.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he would maintain neutrality on the Russia-Ukraine war and that this was not Brazil's problem.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que nao toma partido na invasao russa da Ucrania
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he would maintain neutrality on the Russia-Ukraine war and that this was not Brazil's problem.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs of the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting in a major Brazilian outlet; strong but secondary and the article reflects the president's own remarks.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 while the invasion was ongoing.
contrary_evidence: Brazil also voted against Russia at the UN, so Bolsonaro's neutrality line was not the whole government posture.

evidence.claim: Brazil condemned North Korea's ICBM launch as destabilizing and a violation of UN Security Council resolutions, and urged adherence to the CTBT and NPT.
evidence.title: Brazil officially condemns the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile by the DPRK
evidence.excerpt: Brazil condemned North Korea's ICBM launch as destabilizing and a violation of UN Security Council resolutions, and urged adherence to the CTBT and NPT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Brazilian government statement on a major international-security event.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to Brazil's lawful-security posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government statement under Bolsonaro's administration; not a direct personal Bolsonaro quote.
contrary_evidence: This shows norm enforcement, not direct management of a live interstate conflict.

evidence.claim: Brazil said a humanitarian resolution should include a cessation of hostilities, humanitarian access, and adherence to international humanitarian law, and it abstained because the draft lacked a ceasefire reference.
evidence.title: Brazil abstains on humanitarian-protection draft in the Security Council, citing lack of ceasefire language
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said a humanitarian resolution should include a cessation of hostilities, humanitarian access, and adherence to international humanitarian law, and it abstained because the draft lacked a ceasefire reference.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN Security Council record with a detailed Brazilian explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian government position under Bolsonaro; not a personal Bolsonaro statement.
contrary_evidence: The abstention shows a more cautious peace posture than a simple yes vote would have, so it cuts both ways.

evidence.claim: Brazil said the Ukraine referenda escalated the conflict, were not a real expression of local will under war conditions, and reiterated its call for an immediate ceasefire and peace negotiations.
evidence.title: Statement by the Permanent Representative of Brazil to the United Nations, Ambassador Ronaldo Costa Filho, at the UNSC meeting on Ukraine - September 27th, 2022
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said the Ukraine referenda escalated the conflict, were not a real expression of local will under war conditions, and reiterated its call for an immediate ceasefire and peace negotiations.
evidence.source_locator: Statement body on the Brazilian UN mission page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-ministry publication of Brazil's UN statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian diplomatic line under Bolsonaro; not a personal Bolsonaro quote.
contrary_evidence: Brazil's later abstention on a related resolution shows the government tried to balance territorial-integrity language with negotiation language.

evidence.claim: Brazil abstained on the General Assembly resolution condemning the annexation of Ukrainian regions, and Brazil's representative said the calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities were left out of the draft.
evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation's Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
evidence.excerpt: Brazil abstained on the General Assembly resolution condemning the annexation of Ukrainian regions, and Brazil's representative said the calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities were left out of the draft.
evidence.source_locator: Discussion after the vote, including Brazil's explanation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly record with Brazil's explanation of abstention.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian government position under Bolsonaro's presidency.
contrary_evidence: The same record also shows Brazil reaffirming respect for territorial integrity, so this is not a pro-Russia statement.
